create.name: Great Lake Zen Center
create.bio:
The Great Lake Zen Center is a Korean Zen sangha based in the Milwaukee area of Wisconsin and affiliated with the Kwan Um School of Zen. It follows the teaching of Zen Master Seung Sahn, who brought his style of practice to America in the 1970s, and its core instruction is his question 'What am I?', held as a 'don't know' mind in every situation. Zen Master Dae Kwang, a former abbot of the Kwan Um School, guided the community from its start in 1995 until he retired in 2025.

Today Rebecca Otte, JDPSN, is guiding teacher: she leads retreats, gives kong-an interviews and sets the sangha's direction, while Susi Childress serves as co-abbot alongside a group of dharma teachers who lead the sittings. In-person practice takes place on Thursday evenings at the Unity Center on North 73rd Street in Wauwatosa, where newcomers can attend an Introduction to Zen on the first Thursday of most months. Two further sittings each week, on Tuesday evening and Saturday morning, are held on Zoom, with links shared through the group's mailing list. The centre also marks Buddhist holidays with ceremonies and holds weekend silent retreats with bowing, chanting, walking meditation and work practice.
